about: Downtown skyline identities. Placement = OpenStreetMap outline (ODbL) or City of Austin 2023 footprint; heights = cited sources; tower plan sizes inside block outlines, setbacks, crowns and palettes are ESTIMATES from reference photographs (not shipped) and architect/owner pages. Colours are sRGB 0-255 eyeballed from daylight photos, not measured. Used by tools/extension/bake-downtown.py (geometry) and lib/campus/extension/downtown/landmarks.ts (crowns).

landmarks.name: Waterline
landmarks.heightBasis: 1,025 ft completed height, DPR Construction completion release (2026-08-28); KPF design figure 1,022 ft. Frame crown counts within the 312.4 m overall.
landmarks.evidence: Photo: slender rectangular shaft; lower hotel/office half glass with white horizontal slab bands, recessed dark reveal at the transition, upper residential half a white frame grid with staggered windows, flat top with an open white crown frame. Tower plan = OSM building:part 'Bosque Residences' (way 1213966766); podium = OSM site outline, height estimated.

landmarks.name: Sixth and Guadalupe
landmarks.heightBasis: 865 ft / 263.65 m overall per general contractor J.E. Dunn (primary source, used). Wikipedia lists 875 ft / 266.7 m; the 3 m difference is unexplained by either source (possibly a different top/grade definition - inference only). Parapet crown counts within the 263.65 m.
sources: Wikimedia Commons File:Sixth and Guadalupe, Austin, TX.jpg (reference only)
landmarks.evidence: Photo: opaque parking podium, wider glazed office block, narrower dark-blue residential shaft with a recessed vertical balcony slot; three stacked volumes narrowing upward. Tower plan sizes estimated (centred in the OSM block outline).

landmarks.name: The Republic
sources: Wikimedia Commons File:Downtown Austin Skyline - Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge (54987518915).jpg (reference only)
landmarks.evidence: Photo from the Congress Avenue Bridge: blue glass tower tapering slightly with a sloped (chamfered) crown face. Tower plan, podium height and crown slope estimated.

landmarks.name: The Independent
sources: Wikimedia Commons File:The Independent from the Stacks Austin Texas 2023.jpg (reference only)
landmarks.evidence: Photo: five stacked residential blocks shifted alternately along the long axis ('Jenga'), white frames with glass and inset balconies. Shift distances estimated.

landmarks.name: The Austonian
landmarks.heightBasis: 683 ft, 56 floors, 2010 (Wikipedia list); 2017 USGS LiDAR tiers + City 2023 MAX_HEIGHT. Overall height includes the crown; LiDAR/City body is clamped below the crown base.
sources: Wikimedia Commons File:TheAustonian.jpg and Downtown Austin Skyline - Lady Bird Lake (54987239041).jpg (reference only)
landmarks.evidence: Photos: slender rounded-end blue glass tower over a pale precast podium; the crown curves up into a thin fin at one end. Massing from LiDAR tiers; crown and colours estimated.

landmarks.name: Frost Bank Tower
landmarks.heightBasis: 516 ft, 33 floors, 2004 (Wikipedia list); 2017 USGS LiDAR tiers + City 2023 MAX_HEIGHT. Overall height includes the crown; LiDAR/City body is clamped below the crown base.
landmarks.evidence: Photo: blue-green reflective glass with stepped setbacks, a folded pyramidal crown with sharp spires, buff limestone podium. Spire geometry estimated.

landmarks.name: 360 Condominiums
landmarks.heightBasis: 581 ft incl. mast, 45 floors, 2008 (Wikipedia list); LiDAR tiers + City 2023. Overall height includes the crown; LiDAR/City body is clamped below the crown base.
landmarks.evidence: Photo: warm beige concrete frame with curved glass balconies, stepped top and a slender mast.

landmarks.name: Block 185
landmarks.heightBasis: 591 ft / 180 m per architect Pelli Clarke & Partners (primary, used; STG Design executive architect). Wikipedia lists 577 ft / 175.9 m (possibly roof vs. overall; inference only).
sources: Wikimedia Commons Block_185_from_Lady_Bird_Lake.jpg, Downtown Austin Skyline - Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge (reference only)
landmarks.evidence: Photos: sail-shaped office tower; the lake-facing (south) side curves up in stepped white terrace bands to a peak on the north side; glass with white slab edges. Curve, low height and plan estimated.

landmarks.name: Fairmont Austin
landmarks.heightBasis: 591 ft / 180 m overall including the ~170 ft / 52 m spire (Wikipedia list) => main roof ~128 m (roofM, derived). Overall height includes the mast.
landmarks.evidence: Photo: dark blue-grey glass slab with a recessed vertical slot and a tall thin rooftop spire. Slab plan estimated.

landmarks.name: Indeed Tower
landmarks.evidence: Photo: blue reflective glass tower of folded, angled planes with a chamfered top. Plan and fold estimated.

landmarks.name: Spring
landmarks.heightBasis: 434 ft, 43 floors, 2009 (Wikipedia list); LiDAR tiers + City 2023. Top tier set to the published height (City MAX_HEIGHT can include rooftop equipment).
landmarks.evidence: Photo: slender teal-blue glass residential tower with a white frame band on one face.

landmarks.name: One American Center
landmarks.heightBasis: 401 ft, 32 floors, 1984 (Wikipedia list); LiDAR tiers + City 2023. Top tier set to the published height (City MAX_HEIGHT can include rooftop equipment).
landmarks.evidence: Photo: cream precast/stone with dark punched windows and a stepped 'wedding-cake' top (stepping captured by LiDAR tiers).

landmarks.name: 111 Congress
landmarks.heightBasis: 398 ft, 30 floors, 1987 (Wikipedia list); LiDAR tiers + City 2023. Top tier set to the published height (City MAX_HEIGHT can include rooftop equipment).
sources: Wikimedia Commons File:Downtown Austin Skyline - Lady Bird Lake (54987239041).jpg (reference only)
landmarks.evidence: Photo: rose granite with punched dark windows and a steep pitched/stepped top.

heightPolicy: heightM = published OVERALL height (architectural top including crown, spire or mast) above the lowest terrain under the footprint; the rendered top (tiers + crown) is asserted equal to it by the bake and by check:downtown. roofM, when given, is the main roof below a mast.
